note: Analyst-grade AML questions. Each case names a published typology, states the detection logic a monitoring rule would encode, and cites its source. Questions are phrased the way an investigator asks them — with a window, a threshold, and more than one condition — rather than as single-fact lookups. Gold tokens come from the planted patterns in gen_duckdb.py (see gold.json 'typologies'); a token may offer '|'-separated alternatives because a channel is equally correctly named by its code or its label. `expect_slots` grades whether the agent resolved the right relationship, independent of whether the final answer happened to be right.

thresholds.ctr_note: 고액 현금거래 보고 (CTR) threshold, KRW 10,000,000. Structuring shapes individual transactions to sit just below it.

cases.source: FinCEN: transactions 'on one or more days for the purpose of evading' the reporting threshold; FFIEC BSA/AML Appendix F red flags
cases.detection_logic: count(deposits) >= 3 AND every amount < CTR threshold AND sum(amount) > CTR threshold AND window <= 7 days
cases.why_it_matters: The individual transactions are each unreportable by design; only the aggregate over a window is suspicious. A rule that inspects transactions one at a time cannot see it.
cases.question: Account 9000100 may be receiving structured deposits. Over the 7 days from epoch 1700000000, how many distinct accounts transferred to it in amounts each below 10000000, and what is the total received?

cases.source: FATF, Professional Money Laundering (2018) — small incoming transfers 'almost immediately wired to another city or country'
cases.detection_logic: many-to-one collection THEN a single outbound transfer within hours of the last deposit, over a cross-border rail
cases.why_it_matters: Collection alone is normal for a merchant account. Prompt onward movement of the collected total is what makes it a conduit.
cases.question: After the last incoming deposit to account 9000100, where did the funds go — which account received the onward transfer, over which channel, and how many hours after that last deposit?

cases.detection_logic: a directed transfer path returning to its origin within N hops, with each hop timestamped later than the previous one
cases.why_it_matters: Funds returning to origin have no economic purpose. Detecting it requires traversal, not aggregation — a relational scan of pairs cannot express the closure condition.
cases.question: Starting from account 9000001, is there a chain of transfers that returns to it within 3 hops? List the accounts on the ring in time order and the channel used at each hop.

cases.source: FFIEC BSA/AML red flags — funds moved out shortly after deposit, little or no balance retained
cases.detection_logic: inbound and outbound within a short window AND retained amount is a small fraction of the inbound
cases.why_it_matters: Balance-holding accounts and conduits look identical on volume. The distinguishing signal is elapsed time between the legs and how little stays behind.
cases.question: Account 9000402 is suspected of being a pass-through. How much did it receive, how much did it send onward, how many hours elapsed between the two transfers, and how much was retained?

cases.source: FATF, ML using New Payment Methods (2010) — wider geographic reach implies higher ML/TF risk; 전자금융거래법 §2 channel inventory
cases.detection_logic: transfers whose channel risk weight is at the maximum, traced outward from a flagged account
cases.why_it_matters: Channel choice is a stronger signal than amount for cross-border layering, and it is the dimension a homogeneous transfer edge discards.
cases.question: Flagged account 9000200 sent transfers over maximum-risk channels. Which accounts received them and over which channel each?

cases.typology: Layering — multi-hop dispersal with a time bound
cases.source: FATF layering; FFIEC red flags on rapid movement through multiple accounts
cases.detection_logic: reachability within N hops AND each hop later in time than the previous, so the chain is causally ordered rather than coincidental
cases.why_it_matters: Reachability alone over-reports on a dense graph. Requiring monotonically increasing timestamps is what turns a path into a plausible flow of funds — and it needs variable-length traversal, which a fixed one-hop template cannot express.
cases.question: Trace the funds from flagged account 9000200: which accounts are reachable within 3 transfer hops where each hop occurs later than the previous one?

cases.source: FATF Professional Money Laundering — money mules acting in concert; FFIEC on multiple account holders working together
cases.detection_logic: a beneficiary with many distinct counterparties whose individual amounts cluster just below the threshold, across cash-like channels
cases.why_it_matters: The network shape, not any single account, is the evidence. This is a degree question over a filtered edge set.
cases.question: Which channels were used for the sub-10000000 deposits into account 9000100, and how many distinct depositors used each?

cases.detection_logic: assert that no single transaction into the beneficiary exceeded the threshold, while the aggregate did
cases.why_it_matters: A control question: if a system reports the aggregate as a single large transaction it has mis-modelled the typology. Confirming the maximum stayed below the threshold is what proves evasion rather than a large legitimate payment.
cases.question: For deposits into account 9000100 during the 7 days from epoch 1700000000, what was the largest single amount, and did any single deposit reach 10000000?
